deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. It continues a set of lecture notes on ancient history and geography, under the heading 'Geschichte von Ägypten / Kurze Uebersicht der Geographie von Aegypten' begun on the previous page. The hand is a cursive German student-style hand, and the content reads like notes from a Göttingen-style universal-history lecture; the previous page mentions Gatterer. It is doubtful that Gauss wrote it.

Content, in order:
(1) Egypt is said to be 2/3 the size of Germany (previous page) and 100 German miles long. Its width is not uniform. By far the greater part is sand and stony mountain land, and fertility depends on the Nile.
(2) A remark that some aspect of Egypt (probably its history) belongs among the most remarkable on earth.
(3) On the climate: in Lower Egypt it rains occasionally, in Upper Egypt seldom.
(4) Lake Moeris is singled out as one of the greatest works of the Egyptians. It was meant as a reservoir for Nile water, had 40 German miles of circumference and over 300 feet of depth. A natural valley was used, so that only part had to be dug out.
(5) Heading 'I Ober Aegypten': it was cultivated earliest (or most) and had the first (or most) cities. The capital is Thebes. Each column of the main temple was 50 ft high and 30 ft in circumference.
(6) Heading 'II Mittel Aegypten': it extends to the point where the Nile divides into 7 arms. The capital is Memphis, and the city extends southward (continued on the next page with the temple of Vulcan/Apis, the pyramids and the labyrinth).

The only numerical content is descriptive data of the kind found in Herodotus (II.149: Moeris 3600 stadia in circumference, 50 fathoms deep), filtered through 18th-century German textbooks. No computation or derivation is performed, so nothing needs to be filled in.
errors: No mathematical errors, since there is no mathematics.

Historical/factual: the classical figures for Lake Moeris (Herodotus: 3600 stadia circumference, 50 orgyiai ≈ 300 ft depth) are exaggerated, and modern scholarship regards Moeris as the natural Faiyum lake (Birket Qarun) with Middle Kingdom water-control works. These are the lecture's claims, not the writer's slips.
'Mittel Aegypten' is described as extending to where the Nile divides into 7 arms. This reflects the classical seven Delta mouths; the figure is traditional rather than precise.

results.what: Descriptive geography/history of ancient Egypt: size, climate, Lake Moeris as an artificial reservoir, Thebes and its temple columns, Memphis
results.usually_credited_to: Herodotus (Histories II), transmitted via 18th-century Göttingen historians such as Gatterer

deep.surprise_reason: The page holds non-mathematical lecture notes on Egyptian geography and history, probably not even in Gauss's hand. There is no mathematical content of any kind.

checkable.asserts: 50 fathoms (orgyiai) at 6 feet each gives the stated 300 ft depth of Lake Moeris, consistent with Herodotus' figure
3600 stadia at roughly 90 stadia per German mile gives about 40 German miles circumference, consistent with the stated figure (approximate conversion)

transcription_corrections: Line 4: 'hört zu den merkwürdigsten' should read 'gehört zu den merkwürdigsten'. The subject ('östliche Seite') is uncertain and possibly 'Geschichte'.
Line 6: 'hat viel [-vor-] Sie[?] davon von dem nördlichen[?]' is garbled. The image shows something like 'hat viel ~~vor~~[...] davor vor dem nördlichen', which is uncertain.

Line 8–9: 'Unter den Thieren ist besonders der See[?] Mäuse[?] berühmt' should read 'Unter den Seen ist besonders der See Möris berühmt'. The context is a reservoir for Nile water, and the next page mentions the 'Mörissee'.
Line 10: 'Eine der größten Natur und[?] Anlagen' is probably 'Eins der größten Werke und Anlagen der Aegypter'.
Line 13–15: probably 'Hierzu war ein natürliches Thal, so daß bloß noch einiges Erdreich weiter aus zu graben [war]' (tentative).

Upper Egypt section: likely 'Ober Aegypten wurde am ersten kultivirt und hatte die ~~meisten~~ ersten Städte' (interlinear correction). The transcription's '[-meisten-]{+meisten+}' is self-contradictory.
'Die Hauptstadt ist Theben' is correct as transcribed; 'Memphis' is underlined in the original.
